title: Effect of the Met23Leu Mutation in the KCNE2 Auxiliary Subunit on the KCNH2 Channel Protein Surface Expression
content: Congenital LQTS is the most common form of cardiac channelopathy. It is characterized by asynchronous and delayed ventricular repolarization, predisposes to a high risk of ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. Although this type of channelopathy is mainly associated with mutations in genes encoding the pore-forming subunits of ion channels, in about 30% of patients they are not detected during screening. In addition, quite a large number of cases have been described in which members of the same family, carriers of identical pathogenic variants in ion channel genes, have different clinical manifestations of LQTS ranging from mild to extremely malignant. One of the explanations of this phenomenon is the influence of modulator proteins on channel functions [1]. Mutations in modulator proteins can alter their interaction with ion channels [2, 3]. The GnomAD database [4] has data on some mutations in the Yotiao and KCNE (Mirp) modulator proteins, but the physiological manifestations of these mutations have hardly been described.
